barber.intro: Learn barbering from consultation to finished cut. Master clipper work, razor lines, and the hygiene standards that build a reputation.

skillDomains.name: Consultation
skillDomains.description: Understand the client's hair and what they want.

skills.name: Hair Assessment
skills.description: Every head is different. Read it before you cut.

modules.title: What to check
modules.content:
Before any cut

  • Hair type — fine, medium, coarse; straight, wavy, curly, kinky
  • Density — how much hair on the head
  • Growth pattern — cowlicks, whirls, direction of growth
  • Hairline — natural shape, receding, or thinning
  • Scalp — any cuts, infections, or conditions

Why it matters

Two clients can ask for the same cut. On one it looks great; on the other it looks wrong. The difference is hair type and growth pattern.

modules.title: The consultation conversation
modules.content:
Five questions

  1. What style do you want? (Ask for photos)
  2. How do you usually wear your hair day to day?
  3. When was your last cut?
  4. Any areas you want to keep longer or shorter?
  5. Any irritation, sensitivity, or allergy?

The mirror test

Before cutting, use a mirror to show the client the current shape. Point out areas that will need adjustment. Agree on what the finished cut will look like. This prevents surprises.

steps.q: A client brings a photo of a hairstyle but their hair is much thinner than the model's. What do you do?
o: Cut it exactly like the photo
Explain the difference and offer an adjusted version
steps.f: Match the style to the actual hair.

steps.q: A client has a visible scalp condition (flaking, redness). What do you do?
o: Refer to a doctor before cutting
steps.f: Don't work on irritated or infected scalp.

steps.q: A client isn't sure what they want. What's your approach?
o: Show 2-3 options based on their hair and face shape, let them choose

skillDomains.name: Cutting
skillDomains.description: The core skills — clippers, scissors, and razor work.

skills.name: Clipper Technique
skills.description: The main tool of the modern barber.

modules.title: Clipper fundamentals
modules.content:
The clipper

A motorised cutting tool with adjustable blades or interchangeable guards. Learn the size markings — #1 is very short (3mm), #4 is medium (13mm).

The lever

Adjusts blade position for half-grades (e.g., #2 with lever opened = between #2 and #3).

The technique

  1. Start with a longer guard than you think you need
  2. Cut with the direction of hair growth for even length
  3. Cut against the growth to shorten
  4. Work in sections for consistency
  5. Overlap passes to avoid lines

modules.title: The fade
modules.content:
What a fade is

A gradual transition from very short hair (skin or near-skin) at the bottom to longer hair at the top. There are no visible lines — the transition is smooth.

Steps

  1. Establish the baseline — where the shortest hair ends and skin begins
  2. Create the top length first
  3. Work down in stages — each stage slightly shorter
  4. Blend between stages using lever technique
  5. Finish with a razor for the sharpest line

Common fades

  • Low fade — starts low on the head
  • Mid fade — starts at the temple
  • High fade — starts above the temple
  • Bald fade — blends to actual skin

steps.q: You see lines in your fade after cutting. What went wrong?
steps.f: Lines mean the blending steps were skipped or rushed.

steps.q: Which fade is most difficult to execute?
steps.f: Bald fade requires blending hair to actual skin.

steps.q: A client has a cowlick (whirl) on the crown. How do you handle it?
o: Work with the growth pattern, cut slightly longer around it
steps.f: Cowlicks need longer hair or careful blending.

skills.name: Line & Edges
skills.description: The details that make a cut look sharp.

modules.title: Lining and edging
modules.content:
Lining is the final step of every cut. It's what separates a professional cut from a home cut.

Tools

  • Trimmer or liner clipper
  • Straight razor
  • Shaving brush and cream

What to line

  • Forehead hairline
  • Temple points
  • Around the ears
  • Neckline — creates the finished shape

Technique

  1. Cut the line with the trimmer first
  2. Follow with the razor for the sharpest edge
  3. Shave with the grain, then touch up against
  4. Apply after-shave or balm to soothe

steps.q: A client has a receding hairline. How do you line it?
o: Straighten the line to make it look fuller
steps.f: A slightly straightened line makes a receding hairline look fuller.

steps.q: The client's skin is irritated after lining. What do you do?
o: Apply a soothing balm and skip further razor work
steps.f: Irritated skin needs soothing, not more trauma.

o: At the very base of the neck
Along the natural hairline at the base of the neck

skillDomains.name: Hygiene
skillDomains.description: Clean tools protect clients and your reputation.

modules.title: Blood-borne infections spread through tools
modules.content:
Barbering involves sharp tools near skin. Even small nicks can transfer infections.

What must be sanitised between every client

  • Clippers — brush off hair, oil, spray with disinfectant
  • Scissors — wipe with 70% alcohol between clients
  • Razors — single-use blade, dispose in sharps bin
  • Combs — wash and disinfect
  • Capes — wash or change between clients
  • Chairs — wipe down

Personal hygiene

  • Wash hands before and after every client
  • Wear clean clothing
  • Cover any cuts on your own hands

steps.q: You just finished a client. The clippers look clean. Do you need to sanitise them?
A client nicks their neck while you're lining. What do you do?
o: Stop, clean the cut, apply pressure, disinfect tools, replace blade

steps.q: Where do used razor blades go?
o: Sharps container or sealed rigid box

modules.title: How barbers make money
modules.content:
Speed matters

A barber who cuts in 20 minutes can serve 3x the clients of one who takes an hour. Same skill, 3x the income.

Pricing

  • Basic cut — the entry price, brings them in the door
  • Fade — higher skill, higher price
  • Beard trim — quick add-on
  • Full service (cut + shave + line) — premium price

Retention

A client who returns every 2 weeks for 5 years is 130 visits. That's the real value of each client.

modules.title: Price a full service
modules.prompt: A client wants a bald fade, beard trim, and hot towel shave. Your shop charges: basic cut 5,000 Le, fade premium 3,000 Le, beard trim 2,000 Le, hot towel shave 4,000 Le. Calculate the total. Then describe how you'd manage a queue of 5 waiting clients.
modules.context: Efficiency is what turns barbering into a real business.
rubric: Queue management: acknowledge every waiting client
Work efficiently without rushing the quality
Offer drinks or a seat while they wait
